headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk from Haystack MCP/REST outputs feeding Pipecat shared-bus workflows; no direct evidence of isolation or verification.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Haystack exposes MCP servers and REST APIs, so its outputs can be consumed as structured content. Pipecat supports shared-bus multi-instance state and stdin/stdout transports, which creates a plausible bridge for untrusted content to be reinterpreted as instructions. No direct sandbox evidence exists, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Haystack output is forwarded into Pipecat prompts or tool messages without provenance tagging, injection becomes actionable.
IF a shared bus or clipboard bridges the two agents, attacker-controlled text can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Add provenance labels to all Haystack outputs before Pipecat ingests them.
Strip tool-like markup from retrieved text in Haystack.
Disable automatic prompt concatenation in Pipecat.
Insert a human review step for any cross-agent instruction text.
requires-engineering: enforce schema validation on all inter-agent messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Haystack has broad network egress and can call MCP/REST endpoints; Pipecat touches text, audio, video, images, and conversation state and can send data to many third-party services. A shared workspace is not shown, but the pair can still leak sensitive conversational or retrieved content through default service calls, so the pathway is plausible and not merely theoretical.
conditions: IF Pipecat is configured with any external STT/LLM/TTS provider, conversation content leaves the local boundary.
IF Haystack retrieves sensitive documents and forwards them into Pipecat, those contents can be exposed to downstream APIs.
mitigations: Restrict Pipecat to local-only providers for a quick test run.
Remove sensitive corpora from Haystack retrieval indexes.
Audit outbound endpoints in both configs.
Turn off analytics/telemetry in Pipecat.
requires-engineering: add per-field redaction before any external API call.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Haystack can write through MCP/REST-connected tools, while Pipecat supports shared-bus shared state across multiple instances. That overlap creates a mutable-state conflict risk even without explicit filesystem write fields, because both can act on the same session or downstream resources. Lack of explicit locking evidence keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents target the same shared bus or backing store, writes can race.
IF Haystack-triggered actions and Pipecat session updates occur concurrently, state divergence is possible.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate namespace or topic.
Serialize writes through one coordinator process.
Disable multi-instance sharing during integration tests.
Add optimistic-lock checks on shared records.
requires-engineering: implement distributed locking for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack is a search/RAG system that can emit retrieved facts, and Pipecat is a real-time voice/chat framework that can act on conversational state. If Pipecat treats Haystack output as authoritative, retrieval errors can cascade into spoken or downstream actions. No verification layer is documented, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF Pipecat uses Haystack retrieval results as final answers without verification, errors propagate.
IF downstream actions are triggered from Pipecat conversation state, a bad retrieval can become an operational mistake.
mitigations: Require citation checks before Pipecat speaks or acts.
Add a confidence threshold for Haystack answers.
Log retrieved passages separately from generated responses.
Use a second-pass verifier on critical outputs.
requires-engineering: wire a policy gate before any action-taking step.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and only explicitly touch anonymous usage statistics, audio/video/images/text, conversation state, and analytics. No PHI, EU-only residency, or certification mismatch is documented, so a compliance breach is not established. I do not cite only one agent because the pairwise compliance question needs both profiles to compare data classes and service exposure.
conditions: IF either deployment routes regulated data through external STT/LLM/TTS vendors, compliance scope changes.
IF the operator stores personal data in Pipecat conversation state and indexes it in Haystack, retention obligations may apply.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both systems for a quick baseline.
Document which external vendors Pipecat uses.
Review retention settings for conversation state.
Separate analytics from user content.
requires-engineering: perform a formal data-flow and residency review.
